claim: Conditional static four-byte-record transfer and per-batch bounds, not source reconstruction or equivalence.

domain.raw_transfer: Entry at the selected candidate, original available x86-64 instructions, fixed code, valid state block [Q,Q+120) and nonwrapping stack/return [S-184,S+8); normal call/return state is assumed, not established by stack readability.
domain.zero_guard: First-outer q0 or failed input-order guard performs no table/refill/output-lane access; only state/frame accesses and state writeback. No buffer/table premise is inferred or needed for an unused access.
domain.output_windows: For the entered batch, Oj<=Ej and [Oj,Ej) are genuine nonwrapping writable lane regions. E0/E1/E2 are fixed initial output1/2/3; E3 is initial state+0x70. Their allocation/end meaning is an unverified caller premise.
domain.input_window: L<=initialI0<=initialI1<=initialI2<=initialI3 and immutable nonwrapping [L,initialI3+8) is readable. The three cross-input comparisons are actual guards; L<=I0 and allocation bounds are not checked by the candidate.
domain.table: Immutable readable nonwrapping [T,T+8192), index0..2047. Selected advance bytes are1..2 for the capacity/progress theorem; raw bytes are0..255, without a machine validation of this premise.
domain.BSF: Each of four post-five-shift BSF operands is nonzero in every entered body. Advance1..2 does not imply this; zero has an undefined architectural destination and is outside the proof.
domain.separation: State, active stack/return, immutable code, runtime table, input window and writable output windows have the required separation. Different output lanes are disjoint; successive WORD writes within one lane may overlap for advance1 and are preserved in order.
domain.limits: No recovered runtime table/producer/caller, original source type/ABI/function/algorithm identity, general arbitrary-state safety, whole-call termination, Rust implementation, binary equivalence, function denominator or progress gate is claimed.

boundary_context: PR981 supplies the earlier candidate/FDE context. This tool independently decodes maintained base bytes and does not import its unmerged analyzer.
source_binding: One admitted ELF descriptor/mmap and pre/post full hashes; native tools receive only copied1269B raw bytes. Transient in-place-write atomicity is not claimed.

division_support.meaning: Exact all-u64 floor(d/7) and floor(r/10), by the stated algebra in PROOF.md; source expressions are separately checked.
